memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "What if the number of the righteous is five less than fifty? Will you destroy the whole city for lack of five people?" "If I find forty-five there," he said, "I will not destroy it." Once again he spoke to him, "What if only forty are found there?" He said, "For the sake of forty, I will not do it." - Gen 18:28-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham keeps going. Fifty, then forty-five, then forty. He does not stop at one request but presses on, growing bolder with each appeal to God's mercy. This is persistent prayer - the willingness to keep asking, to press further into God's grace rather than giving up after a single request.

Notice that God never rebukes Abraham for persisting. He does not say, "You already asked; how dare you ask again." With each request, God simply grants the plea. Far from being annoyed by Abraham's persistence, God honours it. Our persistence in prayer does not weary God; it pleases Him.

We often give up too easily in prayer. We ask once, and if the answer doesn't come quickly, we conclude God isn't listening or doesn't care. But Abraham teaches us to keep coming, to keep pressing into the mercy of God, to not lose heart.

Jesus explicitly taught this. He told a parable "to show them that they should always pray and not give up" (Luke 18:1). He urged, "Ask and it will be given to you; seek and you will find; knock and the door will be opened" (Matt 7:7) - words that in the original picture continual asking, seeking, knocking. Do not give up in your praying. Like Abraham, keep coming to the God who welcomes persistent, believing prayer.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you give up too easily in prayer, or do you persist?
- What have you stopped praying about that God may be inviting you to press on with?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You that You welcome my persistent prayers rather than wearying of them. Give me the boldness to keep asking, seeking, and knocking, and not to lose heart. Teach me to always pray and not give up.
Amen.
